chunks: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isam al-Kulayni (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Tamimi, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ilwan, from Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said:

There is not a single believing man or believing woman — from those who have passed since the beginning of time or those who are yet to come until the Day of Resurrection — except that they will serve as intercessors for whoever says in their supplication: 'O God, forgive the believing men and women.'

Indeed, a servant may be ordered to the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, and when he is brought to account, the believing men and women will say: 'O our Lord, this is the one who used to pray for us, so accept our intercession on his behalf.' Then God will accept their intercession for him, and he will be saved.

key_terms.المؤمنين والمؤمنات: The believing men and women — encompasses the entire community of faith, male and female, emphasizing the universality of the teaching.
key_terms.النار: The Fire — refers to Hellfire (Jahannam), the abode of punishment in the afterlife.
key_terms.دعاء: Supplication (du'a) — personal prayer to God, distinct from ritual prayer (salat). Here it refers specifically to praying for the forgiveness of all believers.
key_terms.شفعاء: Intercessors — those who plead on behalf of another before God. In Islamic eschatology, intercession (shafa'ah) is a privilege granted to prophets, imams, scholars, and believers.

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying for the forgiveness of all believers in Islam?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) from his forefathers, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) teaches that every believer — past, present, and future — becomes an intercessor on the Day of Judgment for anyone who regularly includes them in their supplications by saying 'O God, forgive the believing men and women.' This hadith was narrated in al-Saduq's assembly gathering and highlights the mutual spiritual bond among the community of believers across all of history.
